name: STMicroelectronics
exchange: NYSE (also Euronext Paris and Borsa Italiana)

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (ST logo 2020 blue V.svg, the en.wikipedia.org STMicroelectronics infobox logo), saved as the 500 px PNG thumbnail (500x351) because the SVG download was rate-limited (HTTP 429) for this machine

description: STMicroelectronics designs and manufactures chips in its own fabs (an 'integrated device manufacturer') and sells them to more than 200,000 customers in four end markets: Automotive, Industrial, Personal Electronics, and Communications Equipment, Computers and Peripherals. Its products are analog and power chips, MEMS sensors, optical sensors, microcontrollers, automotive and secure processors, and RF/optical parts. Customers buy chips by the piece and, for some, under multi-year capacity reservation and volume commitments; 72% of 2025 revenue was sold directly to equipment makers and 28% through distributors, and Apple alone was 17.7% of revenue. It is in a downcycle with heavy fixed costs: 2025 revenue fell 11% to $11.8 billion and operating income to $175 million (1.5% of revenue) after $376 million of impairment and restructuring and $416 million of unused-capacity charges, though revenue rebounded 26% year on year in Q2 2026.

hq.note: Operational headquarters at 39 Chemin du Champ des Filles, Plan-les-Ouates, Geneva (run through STMicroelectronics International N.V.). Netherlands company with corporate legal seat in Amsterdam and head offices at WTC Schiphol Airport (FY2025 20-F Item 4).

employees.asOf: 2025-12-31 (approximate; the 20-F strategy text says '48,000 creators and makers' without a date)

businessLines.name: Analog products, MEMS and Sensors (AM&S)
businessLines.how: Per-piece sales of chips designed into customers' products (cars, factories, phones, servers); a long design-win to production lag locks in volumes once a part is designed in.
businessLines.description: ST analog and smart-power ICs (automotive, industrial, data-center power, personal-electronics power management), MEMS sensors and actuators, and optical sensing solutions (FlightSense, BrightSense, SafeSense; imaging).

operatingProfit.note: Share is of the four reportable segments' combined $1,149M, before the $(974)M 'Others' items. FY2024 $875M on $5,429M; FY2023 $1,491M on $6,232M.

businessLines.name: Power and Discrete products (P&D)
businessLines.how: Per-piece sales of power and protection chips, plus silicon-carbide devices for electric vehicles; the segment has swung from profit to loss as volumes and prices fell (the 20-F cites lower selling prices and volumes across the company).
businessLines.description: Silicon and silicon-carbide power transistors (MOSFETs, IGBTs, SiC MOSFETs, GaN), thyristors, rectifiers, modules and protection devices.

businessLines.name: Embedded Processing (EMP)
businessLines.how: Per-chip sales of microcontrollers and processors that customers design into products, supported by a software development ecosystem; ADAS parts are sold into automotive programs.
businessLines.description: General-purpose and automotive microcontrollers, connected security products and custom processing products (automotive ADAS).

businessLines.name: RF Optical Communications (RFOC)
businessLines.how: Custom and semi-custom chips made to a customer's specification (silicon photonics, RF-SOI, space parts) sold in volume to a small number of large customers.
businessLines.description: Space, ranging and connectivity products, digital audio and signaling solutions, and optical and RF custom (COT) products, including optical interconnect for data centers and low-earth-orbit satellite parts.

brands.name: Automotive (end market)
brands.note: The 20-F reorganized its sales around five markets (Automotive, Industrial Power and Energy, Industrial Smart Industrials, Personal Electronics, Communications Equipment/Computers/Peripherals) but the passages read give no revenue split by end market.

brands.name: NXP's MEMS sensor business
brands.note: Automotive safety and non-safety sensors and industrial sensors; cash paid $895M in Q1 2026 (6-K); revenue not separately reported
